Q: What is different between App Router and Pages Router in Next.js? A:

To easily understand it, I have created the below table of difference.
Based on your requirements, you can choose the desired router.

Feature App Router Pages Router
Routing type Server-centric Client-side
Support for Server Components Yes No
Complexity More complex Simpler
Performance Better Worse
Flexibility More flexible Less flexible

App Router is the newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.

The official documentation recommends migrating to the new App Router to leverage React's latest features.

Q: Draw a grid with SpriteKit A:

You can implement this manually with SKShapeNode or SKSpriteNode, but if your goal is a reusable, dynamic grid with cell management, positioning and movement support, you might want to use a small helper library instead of rebuilding everything from scratch.

I recently open-sourced a lightweight SpriteKit grid engine that does exactly this:

  • Programmatic rows / columns

  • Fixed cell size

  • Automatic centering

  • Infinite vertical scrolling (optional)

  • Fast cell lookup by row/column

  • Designed for moving sprites between cells

It’s written in pure Swift and works on iOS / macOS / tvOS.

Example usage:

let grid = Grid(
    size: scene.size,
    cellSize: CGSize(width: 40, height: 40)
)

addChild(grid)
grid.build()

Repository:
https://github.com/MitrofD/SpriteGridKit

You can still draw visuals with SKShapeNode if needed, but the grid logic, coordinates and movement are already handled.

Q: JsonPath nested conditions A:

Ah, I see exactly what’s happening here. The problem isn’t your logic—it’s the version of the Java JsonPath library you’re using (com.jayway.jsonpath:json-path < 2.9.0). That version doesn’t fully support nested filters on arrays the way you want, so expressions like ?(@.approvers[*].name=='Luke Skywalker') fail or return weird results.

In JsonPath 2.9.0+, your “generic” query works fine. Here’s the version that would do what you want without specifying array indices:

$.requestedItemsStatus[*].approvalInfo[?(@.approvers[?(@.name=='Luke Skywalker')])]

This basically says: give me every approvalInfo where any approver has the name 'Luke Skywalker'.

Workarounds for older versions (<2.9.0):

  1. Use contains on joined names (hacky):

    $.requestedItemsStatus[*].approvalInfo[?(@.approvers[*].name =~ /.*Luke Skywalker.*/)]

    But this isn’t guaranteed to work in all older Java versions.

  2. Filter manually in Java after parsing: parse the JSON into a List or Map and loop through each approvalInfo, checking the approvers list for the name 'Luke Skywalker'. This is slower but fully reliable.

Recommendation: Upgrade to JsonPath 2.9.0+. It fixes nested array filtering bugs and makes your query work as intended.
